Rozentals created his own OnlyFans account in January 2025 in order to help fund his training programme and he posts videos and pictures on his Instagram account to drive viewers towards the content.
Each athlete on Paddle UK's programme receives an annual grant of Â£16,000 to support their training.
But Rozentals says the programme's funding is nowhere near enough.
"I don't know how much you need but it's certainly not Â£16,000," said Rozentals.
"When you have to cover rent, travel, food... and most athletes who train full-time are all living in London.
"They're very fortunate to have parent backing - I wasn't. I never had the ability to move to London because of financial struggles so I was always doing the travel from the East Midlands, where I live, to London, back-and-forth, back-and-forth."
Rozentals, who won individual C1 silver at the World Under-23 Championships in 2023, is awaiting the outcome of the investigation.
PaddleUK say Rozentals' ban is not disciplinary action, but an "interim action" and a "neutral act designed to protect all parties" and to "safeguard other athletes, staff, and volunteers due to the nature of the allegation".
"The investigation has been referred to independent investigation service Sport Integrity," the governing body said.
It added: "Paddle UK is committed to ensuring a safe and open environment for all, and interim action under the Athlete Disciplinary Policy is only taken where necessary and proportionate."
Paddle UK's Athlete Disciplinary Policy lists "offensive use of social media" and "indecent, offensive or immoral behaviour" as examples of gross misconduct that could lead to de-selection.
Asked if he will stop posting on OnlyFans in order to preserve his place on the programme, Rozentals says he should not have to choose between financial security and his Olympic dream.
"This is the hardest decision that I've ever faced in my life," said Rozentals.
"I came to the realisation about why I started doing this last winter after years of struggle, years of living on the edge, my mum working 90 hours-a-week, having bailiffs at the door.
"I'm going to find a way where we don't have to struggle, where my mum can enjoy her life and I'm able to put everything into this sport because when you're thinking about how to pay the rent this month and you're standing at the start line, that's not very conducive [to performing well].
"It's a tough decision but unless something changes in the way athletes are paid I don't see a way of working with Paddle UK".
Olympic gold medallist Jack Laugher
created his own OnlyFans account
in 2024 to "make ends meet".
The diver won bronze for Great Britain in the men's synchronised 3m springboard in Paris last summer after silver and bronze in Rio eight years earlier.
"There's nothing left to the imagination when you just wear trunks all the time and he just posts pictures of himself as you would see him if he was in a competition," Laugher's father said.

data.article_summary: "Very Small Site" 是一个利用AI在2分钟内创建单页网站的平台，无需注册，适合本地企业、自由职业者、俱乐部和活动页面等。网站简单快速，无复杂后端和数据库，提供免费托管选项，用户也可下载网站自行托管。无需技术技能，通过聊天与AI互动即可更新内容。域名简洁易记，如verysmall.site/yourname。虽然不支持联系表单、电商功能和复杂互动，但对于需要快速上线的简单网站非常理想。使用步骤简单：描述网站需求、AI生成、下载或托管。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“vibe-coded”网页生成工具的实用性、潜在问题及使用体验的讨论

不同观点：
• **justusthane**：认为该工具的示例过于简单，类似于通过模板或WYSIWYG编辑器生成，没有体现出“vibe-coded”的必要性。不过，他也承认某些示例（如带表情雨的页面）展示了工具的灵活性和趣味性。同时，他个人更偏好使用https://mmm.page作为网页生成工具，可能出于对“vibe coding”的偏见。

• **reassess_blind**：认为这个工具的开放性可能导致安全问题，尤其是会有人利用它来创建钓鱼网站或其他恶意内容。由于该工具允许在域上托管任何内容，包括JS，因此存在潜在风险。他引用了文章https://verysmall.site/whycantwehavenicethings来支持其观点。

• **nxobject**：分享了其9岁侄子使用该工具创建网页的积极体验，侄子能够自主创建并展示自己喜欢的内容，体现了工具的易用性和趣味性。他还提出了一种乌托邦式的设想，即在开放互联网上使用此类工具，而非依赖社交媒体平台，可能对孩子的成长更健康。

• **ajoshu**：讨论了自己曾开发类似项目，但最终放弃。他提到其项目中的页面生成后有一个“regenerate”按钮，允许用户进行进一步编辑，增加了灵活性。不过，他最终还是放弃了该项目。

• **sixhobbits**：提供了其他用户使用该工具创建的示例网站链接，展示了该工具在实际应用中的多样性和创造性。

• **stirfish**：对该工具表示赞赏，尤其喜欢用来创建单页网站，但承认自己创建的页面不如其他人有趣。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该工具的潜在安全风险，尤其是被用于创建恶意网站的可能性。
• 用户体验和工具的趣味性、易用性得到了部分用户的积极反馈，尤其是对于年轻用户的创造力激发。
• 部分用户对工具的灵活性和功能性提出了改进建议，如增加编辑功能以提高实用性。

data.title: Hollywood Has Left L.A
data.author: ViktorRay
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述好莱坞影视行业面临的困境以及洛杉矶作为影视制作中心的衰退。演员罗伯·洛讲述了在亚特兰大拍摄时遇到的因缺乏经验丰富的剧组人员而影响拍摄的问题。文章指出，过去十年中，洛杉矶经历了火灾、罢工、疫情、电影院和传统电视衰落以及流媒体 boom 和 bust 等多重打击，导致影视制作大量外流。如今，仅约五分之一的美国电影和电视剧在洛杉矶拍摄，许多即使设定在洛杉矶的电影也在其他地方拍摄。业内人士形容当前的洛杉矶如同一个失去活力和目标的“锈带城市”，制作过程的分散使得好莱坞失去了其传统的物理中心。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：影视作品是否在故事发生地实地拍摄及其影响

不同观点：
• jmugan认为，影视作品应在故事发生的实地拍摄，以保证真实性。他举例指出《The Last of Us》第一集虽然在德州发生，但因不在当地拍摄导致树木等环境细节不准确，并提到其他在洛杉矶发生但不在当地拍摄的电影，认为这是一种浪费。

• spking没有明确表达观点，仅提供了一个存档链接，未直接参与讨论。

• mixmastamyk则关注文章中提到的娱乐业补贴和倾销问题，认为这对其个人有直接影响，并提到有同事十年前因类似原因前往新西兰。他对文章主图表示赞赏，但对文章内容持悲观态度。

补充讨论：
- jmugan强调实地拍摄对提升观众沉浸感的重要性，并通过具体影视作品的例子说明不在实地拍摄可能导致的细节失真。
- mixmastamyk更关注娱乐行业的经济因素，如补贴政策如何影响制作地选择，并通过个人经历（同事迁往新西兰）说明这一现象的影响。
- 争议焦点可能在于影视作品是否必须在实地拍摄才能保证质量和真实性，jmugan支持实地拍摄以保持细节准确，而mixmastamyk则关注经济因素对拍摄地点选择的影响。

Not long ago, Rob Lowe was in Atlanta, shooting a small movie he won’t tell me the name of, when he ran into a problem. “Our camera department was having a hard time getting certain shots because the dolly grip wasn’t hitting his marks,” he says. A Marvel project was filming nearby, along with three or four other large-budget movies, and by the time Lowe and his team arrived, the city’s most experienced crew members were booked elsewhere. “It turned out that our dolly grip had never been on a set before,” Lowe says. “He’d applied for the job because he’d worked a dolly at Costco.”
For 25 years, Lowe has starred on one hit network-TV show after another, including
The West Wing, Brothers & Sisters, Parks and Recreation, Code Black,
and
9-1-1: Lone Star,
which wrapped production on its final season last year. Every single one was shot in the same place TV shows and movies have always been shot and where there’s rarely a shortage of veteran dolly grips: Los Angeles. If it were up to Lowe, he would do all his work in the city where he can sleep in his own bed and be home in time for dinner. “I’ve been fortunate in that I’ve had the ability to mandate it.
9-1-1: Lone Star
was originally going to shoot in Austin, and I told them that wouldn’t work for me,” he says. But lately, filming locally has been more difficult and often flat-out impossible. “The state of the business is so bleak now,” Lowe tells me, “that even
I
am willing to consider shooting outside of L.A. because the opportunities here have just gone away.”
The Hollywood Issue
The Great Realignment
Michael B. Jordan Did the Impossible
Everyone Is Already Using AI (And Hiding It)
It Feels Like 2009 on Dropout
See All
The past decade has been tough on Hollywood — both the industry and the place. L.A. has endured a parade of black-swan catastrophes that have repeatedly upended its signature business, including fires, strikes, COVID, the decline of movie theaters and linear TV, and streaming’s boom and bust. Taken together, these disasters have triggered something like an identity crisis. If you call up a couple dozen executives, agents, directors, producers, writers, actors, and below-the-line artists and ask about the scene on the ground right now, they’ll describe a city detached from its old rhythms and sense of purpose. Today’s L.A., a few say, feels more like a Rust Belt crater than the glamorous capital of the world’s entertainment. “It’s so grim, like a sad company town where the mill is closing,” says one executive. “It’s morose, and everybody’s scared,” says the actor and director Mark Duplass. “It’s a bummer to live here now,” says a writer.
Pieces of the business still hum along in the city, albeit more quietly than they used to. Executives and agents are back in the office, at least the ones who weren’t laid off. Pitching and deal-making continue, though much of that now happens over Zoom. But production — the physical process of turning script pages into movies and TV shows — has largely left town. What began years ago as a trickle has suddenly become an exodus. Today, only about a fifth of American movies and shows are filmed in L.A. According to FilmLA, a nonprofit that tracks permits and has monitored production levels for three decades, 2024 was the worst year on record for local filming, aside from 2020. Even 2023, when the industry was frozen by strikes for nearly six months, saw more activity. And 2025 is off to an even worse start, down 23 percent so far compared with last year. None of 2024’s ten highest-grossing live-action movies was shot in L.A. Nor was a single one of this year’s Best Picture nominees. “These back lots are ghost towns right now,” says
Power
creator Courtney A. Kemp.
Even movies set in L.A. are increasingly filmed elsewhere. Last year, that included
The Substance,
shot in Paris, Antibes, and around Cannes and Nice; and Netflix’s
Carry-On,
which was made in New Orleans. These are scenic places in their own right, of course, but none is quite up to the role. “Making other cities look like L.A. is just not really possible,” says production supervisor and location manager Caleb Duffy. “We’re too identifiable. We’re an international city with too many iconic places to re-create anywhere else. The streets are different; the trees and foliage are different.” Nevertheless, this year, Russell Crowe is reportedly filming the L.A.-set thriller
Bear Country
in Queensland, Australia
.
As the labor of making movies and shows splinters across far-flung cities and countries, Hollywood has become dislodged from its physical home. Some of these new hubs may suit the needs of individual projects, but none of them offers what L.A. did for most of the past century: a stable gravitational center where crews can make a living and the craft can be passed down. data.title: Amelia Earhart's Reckless Final Flights
data.author: Thevet
data.article_summary: 1937年，著名女飞行员阿梅莉亚·埃尔哈特（Amelia Earhart）在尝试进行环球飞行时，在夏威夷的卢克机场发生坠机事故。她的飞机在跑道上失控旋转，幸好没有爆炸，埃尔哈特和两名导航员幸存。埃尔哈特计划成为首位完成环球飞行的女性，但她在起飞时忽视了经验丰富的飞行员保罗·曼兹（Paul Mantz）的建议，导致事故。尽管她早在1928年因成为首位跨大西洋飞行的女性而闻名，但她实际只是乘客。1932年，她独自驾驶单引擎飞机跨越大西洋，尽管条件恶劣且最终降落在爱尔兰的牧场。这次环球飞行计划长达29,000英里，途经豪兰岛等偏远地点，面临巨大风险。然而，成功将带来巨大的商业和媒体机会，NBC和CBS甚至争夺广播权。尽管有导航员陪同，埃尔哈特的准备和练习不足，更多时间花在了宣传和商业活动上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Amelia Earhart的历史地位、飞行技术及其悲剧的讨论

不同观点：
• **[cameldrv]** 认为Earhart的知名度主要得益于宣传机器，并指出公众对其他同样具有历史意义的女性飞行员（如第一位环游世界的女性飞行员）缺乏认识。
• **[cylinder714]** 提供了关于Earhart飞行事故的技术细节，指出其缺乏无线电操作经验是悲剧的重要因素，并提到有人在飞行前拆除了关键的天线设备，认为这是不明智的举动。
• **[WalterBright]** 引用其父亲（一名B-17导航员和职业飞行员）的观点，认为Earhart是鲁莽的飞行员，表达了对其飞行技术的不满，但也表示对另一位女性飞行员Jacqueline Cochran的钦佩。
• **[Kon-Peki]** 提出Earhart被讨论为“鲁莽”主要因为她是女性且失败了，而其他同样失败的男性飞行员却没有受到同样关注，暗示性别因素在其中起到了作用。
• **[0xbadcafebee]** 认为Earhart这样的故事提醒人们两件事：历史创造者往往需要一些“疯狂”，以及无需掩饰英雄的缺陷，因为他们的传奇依然会流传下去。

补充讨论：
• **技术分析**：[a-r-t] 提供了Veritasium关于Earhart最后一次飞行的技术分析视频链接，深入探讨了飞行中的技术问题。
• **历史背景**：[beedeebeedee] 强调了飞行早期阶段的普遍鲁莽性，并通过提到1920年代阿拉斯加的飞行员故事（如Eielson和Wilkins）来对比Earhart的情况，指出当时整个行业都在学习如何让飞行变得更安全。
• **编辑风格批评**：[johnyzee] 对评论中使用变音符号（如"coördinated"）表示不满，认为这是不必要的矫饰。
• **语言问题**：[bauble] 对文章中使用“human navigators”代替“male navigators”表示困惑，认为这是不必要的或错误的措辞。

争议焦点：
• Earhart是否因其性别而被过度批评，以及她的飞行是否真的比同时代的其他飞行员更鲁莽。
• 关于Earhart飞行事故中的技术问题，特别是无线电和天线设备的准备是否充分。

Sparks flew, a wing bent, and the landing gear snapped off as the silver Lockheed Electra 10-E plane smashed into the runway at Luke Field, outside Honolulu. The pilot’s only stroke of luck was that the aircraft, which contained nearly a thousand gallons of fuel, didn’t explode.
The thirty-nine-year-old Amelia Earhart and her crew of two navigators, Fred Noonan and Harry Manning, crawled out of the wreckage, unsettled but otherwise unhurt. They had meant to depart on the second leg of a gruelling voyage: a round-the-world flight that had begun in Oakland, California, and would continue westward, with two dozen or so stops, before ending up back in Oakland. People close to Earhart knew that she wasn’t fully ready for a challenge of this magnitude, and so a work-around had been devised. An extra crew member with extensive flight experience, Paul Mantz, had joined the flight to Hawaii. On the runway in Oakland, he switched places with Earhart and assumed the throttles during takeoff. She then piloted most of the way to Oahu, but Mantz often took over.
As they approached Luke Field, Mantz sensed that Earhart had “pilot fatigue.” He asked her, “Do you want to land it?”
“No, you land it,” Earhart said.
He did so, then said farewell. Earhart had been able to observe Mantz’s handling of the plane over the Pacific, and from now on she would be the only pilot onboard. Flying the Electra solo wouldn’t be easy. Although the plane had state-of-the-art technology for its time, piloting it demanded constant coördination among the throttle, the rudder, and the control column—especially during takeoff and landing. While taking off on the second leg, Earhart ignored advice that Mantz had given her not to “jockey the throttles”—change the speed to maintain direction and balance—and the plane veered into a violent spin across the runway. The press had assembled to watch Earhart soar, and instead witnessed an embarrassment.
The stakes were huge. Men had been flying around the world since 1924, when a team of eight military officers completed a twenty-seven-thousand-mile journey in a hundred and seventy-five days (with seventy-four stops). Only one pilot had done a solo circumnavigation: a Texan named Wiley Post. In 1933, Post completed a fifteen-thousand-mile journey, traversing Germany, the Soviet Union, Alaska, and Canada. Four years later, a round-the-world flight remained daunting. Earhart planned to have human navigators on board with her, but she’d be the first female pilot to accomplish the feat.
Earhart had become instantly famous in 1928, as the first woman to cross the Atlantic in a plane. But, though she’d been photographed wearing a flight suit and a leather helmet, she was merely a passenger; the plane had actually been piloted by two men, Wilmer Stultz and Louis Gordon. She had since been working on establishing her command of the cockpit. There were plenty of accomplished female pilots who could’ve taken command of a transatlantic flight themselves, and some of these women considered Earhart’s notoriety unearned. In 1932, after logging more flight miles—but not as many as other top female pilots—she flew solo across the Atlantic in a cramped red Vega, a single-engine plane barely insulated against storms and cold temperatures. She fought exhaustion, iced wings, and a broken altimeter. Her intention was to land in Paris, but she ended up in a cow field in Ireland. Earhart approached the experience with an easy, almost reckless, confidence. She’d always been this way; as a girl growing up in the Kansas City area, she jury-rigged a “roller coaster” with steep ramps, then barrelled down it and fell off, only to exult, “This is just like flying!”
A globe-circling flight would be Earhart’s lengthiest journey by far, twenty-nine thousand miles hugging the equator. This wasn’t mere hopping among landmasses, as with Post’s route. Her path had been ambitiously charted to include a refuelling stop on Howland Island, a speck between Hawaii and Australia. A pilot making such a journey needed to be in excellent shape, with sufficient strength and stamina to manage the controls in turbulence, particularly during long hours in a cockpit with no autopilot. The dangers were extraordinary: enormous stretches over open ocean, unpredictable weather, extended isolation, intense psychological pressure. Yet the rewards promised to be substantial, from marketing opportunities to media attention. NBC and CBS were fighting over the rights to exclusive broadcasts.
Noonan and Manning had agreed to accompany Earhart nearly the whole way. They were excited to be associated with her glamour, but they also considered the job a risk. Rather than spending time practicing in the powerful Electra, Earhart had been crisscrossing the country, giving lectures, making sponsorship appearances, and attending promotional events. For a while, she had a gig as the aviation editor at
Cosmopolitan

data.author: seveibar
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者使用TypeScript开发的一个3D SVG渲染器，能够在不进行光栅化的情况下实现纹理的透视投影。由于SVG原生不支持透视变换（仅支持仿射变换），作者通过将图像细分并为每个子区域应用局部仿射变换，成功模拟了透视效果。通过增加细分数量，投影效果更加平滑，最终在512个子区域时几乎看不出区别。该方法避免了光栅化，并保持了SVG文件较小。该渲染器旨在帮助渲染使用React制作的电路板，并计划用于开源项目中，方便在GitHub上审核设计更改。

How can you make affine transformations (the only ones SVGs are capable of) resemble perspective transformations?
Seve

I’ve been building a
vanilla 3D object to SVG renderer in Typescript
to help render
circuit boards that are made in React
and discovered an interesting trick to keep the SVGs small while getting approximately-correct looking perspective transformations with image textures.
An example circuit board rendered with our vanilla Typescript 3D Renderer. Great for checking sizing! You can see we were able to project the “texture” containing the PCB traces!
SVGs don’t support perspective transforms like CSS (or at least they’re not guaranteed to work in image viewers), so we need a way to simulate this perspective transformation without creating a massive SVG. It’s easy to draw the box below, you can just project the face of each side of the cube into a polygon, but mapping the texture to that perspective transform isn’t natively possible!
Perspective transforms in CSS using the transform attribute (from MDN)
So SVGs don’t support perspective transforms, what do they support? SVGs support this nice little transform called an affine transform. This 6 number transform is what you get when you do
transform: matrix(a,b,c,d,e,f)
in CSS. They are super useful for 2D transformations, like panning/scaling/dragging, but can’t really project into 3d.
Possible affine transforms
from wikipedia
This projection isn’t possible with a single affine transform. You also can’t combine affine transformation matrices together to create this shape.
How can we approximate the transform? Here are some ideas I mulled over that could achieve a good result:
Redraw the image with the distortion. This is potentially expensive and means that we can’t use SVGs as the images without converting them to bitmaps. It also means that things might look “fuzzy”
Ray trace everything! By projecting a ray to compute each pixel for the image, I could get a very conventional 3d renderer. This doesn’t achieve my goal of lightweight SVGs though
Subdivide the image and project each subdivision in the most locally-correct affine transformation. Use projected polygon clip paths to cut off the edges of regions.
I was really curious how the last bullet point could work, and I could think of no other ideas that didn’t require rasterization. So with OpenAI O3’s help I implemented it into the vanilla Typescript 3D renderer. To test it, we’re going to project a checkerboard pattern onto a cube.
Cube with no texture
Ok here’s our starting point, 2 subdivisions, the 2 checkboard images with affine transformations.
Two subdivisions with a different affine transformation applied to each image
Not too bad, let’s see it with 4 subdivisions!
Four images with different affine transformations
Looks a bit rough (literally, it looks like it is not a flat surface). Let’s keep going!
Eight images, eight clip paths, still not very smooth!!
16 images, 16 clip paths
Alright let’s go to the end, we want it to look flat!!
512 Images & Clip Paths
At around 512 images, it’s really hard to tell the difference. Awesome! We did image projection without any rasterization!
Now for the exciting part: The SVG isn’t that big! Because we can use the `defs` of the SVG to avoid repeating the image, we only need to define each clip path!
This is the full file for the subdivision-2 cube. The polygons are the sides of the cube. The groups and clip paths are the only things that you need for each subregion.
Here’s a table of the file size as you increase subdivisions. I _think_ some differences in the matrix calculation account for the somewhat weird scaling.
The math is fun but in the age of AI, below our pay-grade!
You can check out the full source code here
!
Relevant snippet from the source where we subdivide and use bilinear interpolation to find the relevant quads
I’m excited to flesh out this 3D renderer because 3D SVGs can make great artifacts on GitHub, we want to make it so that people can easily review changes to circuit boards made with
tscircuit
in pull requests.
A visual snapshot test with a 3D SVG
I hope you enjoyed this neat little 3D trick!
Back to coding…
I’m building an open-source electronics kernel! Also other things!

data.title: LLMs and Elixir: Windfall or Deathblow?
data.author: uxcolumbo
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了大语言模型（LLMs）对Elixir编程语言社区的影响，提出LLMs可能带来的机遇与挑战。作者担心LLMs会导致新手程序员依赖不当的工具，如选择Node.js和Next.js而非Elixir，因为这些是模型更常推荐的。然而，作者也认为，如果LLMs能够有效引导开发者选择适合的工具（如Elixir），那将是积极的。文章进一步分析了两种可能：一是LLMs统一编程语言，二是新手和“氛围编程者”遇到Elixir曾解决的问题。作者倾向于第二种情况，认为只要LLMs能有效支持非主流技术，Elixir社区就能继续繁荣。总体而言，作者对Elixir的未来持谨慎乐观态度，认为LLMs会改变软件开发，但不一定带来负面影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在不同编程语言和框架中的应用效果，特别是Elixir语言的优势与局限。

不同观点：
• ipnon认为，尽管LLM在主流语言如Python和React中生成的代码较多，但Elixir生成的代码更易于理解和修改，且由于其运行时的特性，系统崩溃的可能性较低。Elixir减少了人工检查和修改代码的循环次数。
• CompoundEyes分享了使用Phoenix框架和Elixir的积极体验，特别是在TDD（测试驱动开发）和处理复杂项目时的稳定性。他们认为，Elixir和Phoenix在项目复杂度增加时仍能保持方向感，而其他框架往往容易迷失。
• rickcarlino对Elixir作为通用编程语言提出质疑，认为它更适合于服务器应用开发，而非其他类型的应用。他指出，Elixir及其社区主要关注客户端/服务器用例，因此应被视为一种专用语言。
• miki123211提出，未来的编程语言需要针对LLM和LLM开发者进行设计，以适应第三波语言发展潮流。
• fernmyth认为，LLM对编写新语言（如Crystal）的项目有很大帮助，特别是在编写缺失库和解释概念方面。
• jtbayly分享了自己在不太了解Elixir的情况下，通过LLM的帮助成功编写应用的经历，认为LLM提供了另一种视角，有助于发现和解决问题。
• the_duke主张使用严格类型系统的语言（如Rust）进行代理编码，因为这些语言更容易验证输出正确性，并减少LLM生成无意义代码的可能性。
• aczerepinski指出，LLM在处理某些Elixir库时会遇到困难，需要人工干预，而他们在其他语言（如Go/Ruby和JS/TS）中的表现更好。
• artem2471认为，LLM在处理具有强大静态分析和优秀编译器UX的语言（如Elm和Rust）时表现良好。
• Dowwie认为，Claude模型在Elixir和Erlang能力方面领先，Elixir在工作流和利用硬件资源方面表现出色，但Python在市场上更受欢迎。
• tobyhinloopen指出，功能编程语言因无隐藏副作用，非常适合LLM处理，并建议Elixir/Phoenix提供“LLM文档”。
• badsectoracula建议，每个库可以包括一个专门为LLM设计的简要文档，以指导正确使用。
• rhgraysonii分享了自己长期使用LLM编写Elixir的积极经验，并表示愿意回答其他人的问题。

补充讨论：
• 1oooqooq幽默地指出，有些人会尽量避免阅读手册，依赖LLM帮助。
• bad_haircut72提到，通过Tidewave工具，LLM可以进行自己的REPL循环调试和调查，认为Elixir在LLM时代将蓬勃发展。

争议焦点：
• Elixir是否应被视为通用编程语言，还是更适合特定用途（如服务器应用）的专用语言。

Will “AI” force a convergence towards the tools it  “knows” best?
The argument goes like so: Now that you have a bunch of folks who are “vibe coding”, they will just do whatever ChatGPT or Claude tell them to do. They will also be evaluating things almost solely against “how well did my ‘AI’ do with it” for making decisions going forward. For Elixir, this sounds like bad news bears. Here is a portion of a very long-winded response from ChatGPT when I asked it how I could “build a website like Amazon”.
Oh no! I in my ultimate wisdom know that this is nowhere close to the best stack for the job. But the noobs won’t know that at all! Let’s say instead they’ve heard of Elixir on a blog post, or they saw this article topping the hacker news charts 🤞 (hi mom!).
I’m in this unique situation where time-to-market happens to matter. Also what do you mean “learning curve”, you’re supposed to do the learning for me. Thanks Chat, you really helped me dodge a bullet here, guess I’ll stick with Node & Next.js, thanks! 🥰
Lets not beat a dead straw man
Mixing metaphors like a boss. While I’m sure the above scenario will play out countless times, at the end of the day this
isn’t new
. Theoretically this all goes one of two ways.
“AI” is able to overcome the fundamental issues with any tool, thus equalizing effectively all programming languages.
Vibe coders & new programmers working with LLMs hit the same walls that drove Elixir to exist in the first place.
In my opinion, both of these realities are “good news” in a way. In scenario 1, we’ve got magical mystery robots and they’ll just create the one programming language to rule them all and now we all have infinite automation in our pockets. Let’s talk about scenario 2, the one I find far more likely.
Hitting Walls
It’s no surprise that these things will mirror popular opinion. We can finagle our way there. This is a fresh prompt.
After giving me a bunch of sensible recommendations like using a CDN, horizontally scaling, using background jobs, migrating from Vercel to ECS, and scrolling past the recommendations to rewrite in Go and Rust, we finally found what we were looking for 🥹.
This brings us to a crucial realization: if LLMs can successfully guide someone toward Elixir when the use case demands it, then perhaps the real challenge isn't LLM bias toward mainstream tools - it's making sure LLMs can work effectively with our tools to enable developers to make that choice.
Alright, I’m up and running. Not sure how this would cost someone $10k on Vercel but I’m sure someone could find a way.
So let's test this theory. If I take Claude's advice and decide to explore Elixir, how well can it help me actually build something?
Not only does it work, but it does it effectively the same way that I personally would have done it if given the same task.
LLMs are quite good at translation. Where they often fall down with invention, this kind of thing is their bread and butter. It even kept it compatible with the node server I started with.
Plus some goodies:
Now, this doesn’t necessarily mean that non-mainstream technologies will be naturally surfaced over time, but, well…
If LLMs never get good enough to do things like troubleshoot esoteric technology and learn new things that weren’t in their training set, then they’ll fade into irrelevance anyway. So let’s extend this line of thinking out. If you think (like we probably all do) that your soup du jour is better than the other guy’s, then guess what? Either the LLMs will get “smart” enough to
realize it too
, or you’ll
eat all the vibe coder’s lunch because they never figure it out.
Okay, so we’re all good then?

44186496.article_summary: 文章探讨了大语言模型（LLMs）对Elixir编程语言社区的影响，提出LLMs可能带来的机遇与挑战。作者担心LLMs会导致新手程序员依赖不当的工具，如选择Node.js和Next.js而非Elixir，因为这些是模型更常推荐的。然而，作者也认为，如果LLMs能够有效引导开发者选择适合的工具（如Elixir），那将是积极的。文章进一步分析了两种可能：一是LLMs统一编程语言，二是新手和“氛围编程者”遇到Elixir曾解决的问题。作者倾向于第二种情况，认为只要LLMs能有效支持非主流技术，Elixir社区就能继续繁荣。总体而言，作者对Elixir的未来持谨慎乐观态度，认为LLMs会改变软件开发，但不一定带来负面影响。

data.title: Authentication with Axum
data.author: mattrighetti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了使用Axum框架和Askama模板实现用户认证的方案，重点介绍了如何通过导航栏按钮反映用户的登录状态。当用户已认证时显示"Profile"按钮，未认证时显示"Login"按钮。核心思路是利用 cookies 进行用户认证，cookies 通过设置 `HttpOnly`、`Secure` 和 `SameSite` 等属性增强安全性，防止XSS、CSRF等攻击。文章还提到可以使用 `axum-extra` 包中的 `CookieJar` 来简化 cookies 的操作，并建议使用 JWT 作为认证 tokens，通过设置短期有效的 JWT 和长期有效的刷新 token 来确保持续性和安全性。最后，文章简要描述了实现登录端点的步骤，包括验证用户凭据并为其设置两个 cookies（JWT 和刷新 token）。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• Goofy_Coyote认为，HttpOnly属性并不能完全"中和"XSS攻击。它仅能防止JavaScript读取cookie，但无法阻止恶意脚本代表用户发送请求或执行其他恶意操作。Goofy_Coyote强调，防御XSS需要结合输入验证、输出编码和内容安全策略（CSP）等多重措施。

• Skwee357讨论了单页应用（SPA）时代前后，会话管理和认证方式的变化。他疑惑为什么要将JWT存储在cookie中，而不是使用Axum提供的签名和私有cookie来存储JWT。

• Johnduhart认为，使用JWT存储在cookie中是一种优势，因为不需要在服务器上存储会话数据。然而，他质疑这种方法在处理刷新令牌和重新签发JWT时的复杂性，认为使用传统会话可能更简单。

• 0x457强烈反对将JWT存储在cookie中，认为这只会带来JWT的所有缺点而没有任何优点。他建议使用常规会话管理，因为这样更有效率，且减少客户端请求的数据量。

• Ripley12分享了使用Axum实现身份验证的实际经验，认为这是一个很好的学习体验，但希望未来能使用更简化的工具包。

• Mrbluecoat提到Neon Auth作为一种替代方案，质疑当前讨论的方法是否优于Neon Auth。

补充讨论：
• Goofy_Coyote提供了具体的例子，说明恶意脚本如何利用HttpOnly保护下的cookie进行攻击，如发送请求添加管理员用户、重写DOM以伪造登录页面等。
• 讨论中涉及的争议焦点在于JWT与传统会话管理的优劣，特别是存储JWT在cookie中的合理性，以及与服务器会话管理相比的复杂性和效率问题。
• 不同的技术选择（如Axum、Neon Auth）也被提及，显示出社区对多种解决方案的关注和比较。

Authentication with Axum May 3, 2025 Discuss on HN Consider this scenario: you’re building a website that has a classic navbar at the top, this navbar has a button that reflects the user authentication status, showing a "Profile" button if the user is authenticated and showing a "Login" button in case the user is unauthenticated. This is a very common scenario, let’s sketch something quick using axum and askama. {% block title %}{% endblock %} {% block head %}{% endblock %}
{% if ctx.authed %} Profile {% else %} Login {% endif %}
{% block content %} {% endblock %} This will be our layout.jinja file that we can build upon. The template above would be served by an endpoint that looks like the following #[derive(Debug, Default)] pub struct Context { authed: bool, } #[derive(Template)] #[templage = "layout.jinja"] struct HomeTemplate { ctx: Context }; pub async fn home() -> impl IntoResponse { HtmlTemplate( HomeTemplate { ctx: Context::default() } ).into_response() } We have something to work with, all is missing is a way derive a Context from a user’s HTTP request. I’d argue the simplest way to handle user authentication if you’re doing SSR is using cookies. Cookies are a cornerstone of backend authentication because they’re reliable, browser-managed, and can be hardened with specific attributes to mitigate common security risks. Here’s why: HttpOnly Attribute: Prevents client-side JavaScript from accessing the cookie, neutralizing XSS attacks. If an attacker injects malicious scripts, they can’t steal your session cookie. Secure Attribute: Ensures the cookie is only sent over HTTPS, protecting it from interception on insecure networks (e.g., public Wi-Fi). SameSite Attribute: Mitigates CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) by controlling when cookies are sent in cross-origin requests. SameSite=Strict blocks cookies in requests from external sites, while SameSite=Lax allows safe methods like GET. Expiration and Domain/Path Scoping: Cookies can be set to expire after a session or a fixed time, reducing the window for misuse. Scoping to specific domains and paths (e.g., domain=api.example.com , path=/auth ) limits their exposure. Signed Cookies: Frameworks often support signing cookies with a secret key, ensuring they haven’t been tampered with on the client side. This is a typical reponse that uses the Set-Cookies header to instruct the browser to set those cookies HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: application/json Set-Cookie: session=xyz123; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=86400; Path=/; Domain=api.example.com When configured correctly, cookies are a fortress for storing session IDs, JWTs, or other authentication tokens in SSR apps. They’re automatically sent by the browser with every request, simplifying server-side validation compared to managing tokens in localStorage or HTTP headers. Axum provides a cool axum-extra crate that makes it easy to work with them. That crate contains a very useful extractor called CookieJar that exposes a very minimal interface to .add and .remove cookies for a user. This is the utility function I use to generate a default cookie pub(crate) fn default_cookie<'a>( key: &str, token: String, duration_hrs: i64 ) -> Cookie<'a> { Cookie::build((key.to_string(), token)) .path("/") .http_only(true) .max_age(Duration::hours(duration_hrs)) .secure(if cfg!(debug_assertions) { // Safari won't allow secure cookies // coming from localhost in debug mode false } else { // Secure cookies in release mode true }) .build() } I won’t get sucked into the session ID vs. JWT argument, but honestly, using JWTs in cookies is a win because you don’t have to fuss with storing session data on the server. Jwt are usually very short-lived, they shouldn’t last for long periods of time and they must be renewed frequently for security purposes. For that reason you usually issue two different cookies: jwt: short-lived token containing information about a user in json format, signed with a secret key so you know you were the one who issued it refresh token: a longer-lived token with which you can request new jwts Now that we’ve covered the cookies and jwt basics, let’s start by implementing a standard login endpoint with which users can be given these two cookies. #[derive(Debug)] struct LoginData { username: String, password: String } pub async fn login( State(app): State, jar: CookieJar, // CookieJar is available in axum_extras Form(LoginData { username, password }): Form ) -> impl IntoResponse { // dummy function to get a user let user = match db::user::get(&app.pg_pool, &username, &password).await { None => return Redirect::to("/signup").into_response() Some(user) => user }; // get/create a refresh token for the user let re

data.title: parrot.live
data.author: jasonthorsness
data.article_summary: "parrot.live" 是一个开源项目，旨在通过使用 `curl` 命令在终端中显示动画 Party 鹦鹉。该项目基于 "terminal-parrot"，用户可以通过输入 `curl parrot.live` 来观看动画。项目感谢了贡献者如 jmhobbs 提供的动画帧以及其他测试和反馈人员。此外，项目还提供了更多鹦鹉相关资源的链接，如 cultofthepartyparrot.com 和 parrotsay。技术上，项目主要使用 JavaScript 和 PowerShell 开发，并在 GitHub 上获得了 3.8k 个星标和 180 个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个ASCII动画网站在技术社区引发的讨论，包括技术实现、个人项目回顾、技术问题反馈等。

不同观点：
• **项目成就和趣味性**：
   - [hsx] 分享了自己8年前随手搭建的项目，并提到最近才发现有内存泄漏问题，同时指出项目多年来消耗了大量带宽。
   - [oytis] 赞扬了作者的编程能力，称其为“编码机器”。
   - [90s_dev] 回忆了自己制作的类似趣味项目，一个在测试通过后跳出来的彩虹独角兽。
   - [mathewpregasen] 认为这是Hacker News存在的意义，即分享有趣的技术项目。

• **技术细节和实现方式**：
   - [Liftyee] 提到项目带宽使用情况，并对比了安装软件的麻烦和直接显示字符的安全性。
   - [mtekman] 提到了类似的项目smithers.el，扩展了讨论范围。
   - [sandos] 对项目的技术实现表示好奇，询问是否与curl的默认日志记录有关。
   - [jasonthorsness] 解释了如何正确使用curl命令访问该网站。
   - [troupo] 提到了类似的历史技术，如通过telnet观看ASCII版《星球大战》。

• **技术问题和反馈**：
   - [financypants] 提到访问该网站导致自己的ssh会话崩溃。
   - [donbreo] 报告网站无法访问。
   - [Daviey] 提到网站因为访问量过大而崩溃，出现504网关超时错误。

补充讨论：
• **跨平台问题**：
   - [baalimago] 询问该项目是否能在PowerShell上运行，扩展了项目在不同平台上的适用性讨论。

• **用户体验和趣味项目**：
   - [joshdavham] 询问是否有其他类似的项目，显示出对更多趣味技术项目的好奇心。

争议焦点：
• 项目的技术实现和访问问题引发了讨论，部分用户报告了崩溃和无法访问的问题，而其他用户则分享了类似的趣味项目，显示出对项目实现方式的不同理解和技术挑战。

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了用于自动复制签名的Autopen机器，尤其在NASA宇航员中广泛使用。Autopen通过模板 recreate签名，使宇航员能专注于工作而不被签名请求打扰。NASA常用的是Damilic公司生产的Autopen Model 80，通过Plexiglas模板操作，签名区域约为3" x 1"。尽管效率高，但高速运行可能导致签名潦草。不同模板可快速切换，以生成不同人的签名。Apollo时代的Autopen与真人签名仍有区别，如签名突然停止、线宽不一、线条抖动、位置异常等特征，帮助识别。

Identifying Autopens
1. What is an Autopen?
The Autopen machine is a mechanical device used to automatically recreate genuine-looking signatures of a given person. These machines were first developed around the beginning of the 20th century but only became widely used in the last 60 years or so.
Although most people are unaware of their existence, Autopen machines are widely used by government institutions, businesses and celebrities. Certainly all U.S. presidents since Eisenhower have used them at one time or another (JFK was one of the first big users). In the context of this site obviously the most important users are the NASA astronauts, all of whom were (and still are) given access to these machines and encouraged to use them.
The use of Autopens machines is generally justified by the fact that they allow the signee to spend their time on their job rather than signing autographs or routine documents. In the case of NASA there was no way that the Apollo astronauts could have routinely signed all autograph
requests and still done their jobs so NASA had to choose between refusing all requests or sending out Autopenned signatures.
Choosing the latter option probably made a lot of people happy at the time as the vast majority of recipients would have been unaware that the signatures were not genuine. Even some
astronauts unknowingly ended up with Autopen signatures of their fellow astronauts in their own personal collections.
The most common type of autopen machine used by NASA in the early years was the Autopen Model 80, built by the
Damilic Corporation
of Rockville, Md.
The machine (
right
) resembled a small drafting table, with a mechanical writing arm on one side and an open area beside it for stacking signed and unsigned documents.
An Autopen machine works from a template (or signature matrix) which was created by the Autopen company from a copy of the signee's real autograph.
While
modern Autopen machines
work
from digital patterns, the Apollo-era Autopen templates took the form of a large Plexiglas spiral with indentations in the top surface
which was loaded into the machine onto a turntable situated under the desk top, as shown in the photo below.
A pen, pencil or marker was inserted at the end of the mechanical arm and
letters, photographs, certificates or even books caould then be placed under the pen and the signature would be drawn out on the item at the press of a button.
The Model 80 Autopen machine had a writing area roughly 3" across by 1" high, so a template could incorportate short phrases (e.g. "Best Wishes") or symbols (e.g. the Mercury sigma 7 symbol) alongside the actual signature.
Apparently a skilled operator could turn out thousands of signed items a day if necessary using the machine, although it seems that if run at too high a speed the signatures
could become a bit 'sloppy' (showing the shaky lines mentioned in section 2.3).
Templates could be swapped in and out of the machine easily, allowing a single machine to produce the signatures of multiple persons (e.g. an Apollo crew) or to produce varying versions of the same signature.
Future versions of these machines may be produced which mimic the actual handwriting style of a celebrity (including some 'natural' variation) in order to create 'handwritten' and signed letters at will, but luckily for us the
Apollo-era machines, while impressive, did not write in quite the same way as a human.

data.title: Foam: A free Roam alternative for VSCode
data.author: AbuAssar
data.article_summary:
Foam 是一个基于 Visual Studio Code 和 GitHub 的个人知识管理与分享系统，受 Roam Research 启发。它可以帮助用户组织研究、记录可重新发现的笔记、撰写长文，并可选择将内容发布到网络。Foam 是免费开源的，具有高度可扩展性，用户可以完全掌控自己创建的信息，并自由分享与协作。

主要功能包括：
- 图形可视化：通过图形展示笔记间的联系。
- 链接自动补全：帮助创建笔记间的连接。
- 文件重命名时同步链接：保持笔记的一致性。
- 跨目录唯一标识符：支持同名文件在不同目录中存在。
- 链接预览与导航、笔记嵌入、章节支持、链接别名、模板、反向链接面板、标签浏览面板等功能。
- 支持孤立和占位符面板，帮助管理无链接或无内容的笔记。
- 语法高亮、每日笔记、生成 Markdown 引用等。

Foam 提供了多种命令和快捷方式，帮助用户高效管理知识库，并支持通过图形和反向链接发现笔记间的联系。用户可以根据指南创建一个 Foam 工作区，使用 Markdown 文档记录想法，并通过 Wiki 链接进行连接和浏览。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Foam 作为知识管理工具的优缺点及其与其他工具（如 Obsidian、org-roam）的比较

不同观点：
• [sputknick] 认为 Foam 的 VS Code 集成是其最大的优点，但同时也是缺点。因为作者的笔记中只有三分之一与软件开发相关，所以大部分时间使用 VS Code 显得笨重。他认为如果笔记内容几乎全部与软件开发相关，Foam 才是一个理想的选择。

• [metayrnc] 关注 Foam 是否具备类似 Obsidian 中 Dataview 的功能，并表示如果没有此类功能，会犹豫是否切换到 Foam。这表明用户对数据管理和查询功能的需求是切换工具时的重要考虑因素。

• [fouc] 引用了 Foam 的定义，强调其作为基于 VS Code 的知识管理和分享系统，灵感来源于 Roam Research。这表明该用户可能在简单描述工具的核心特性，而不带有明显的立场。

• [mtzaldo] 提出了一个技术趋势相关的问题，将 VS Code 和 Electron 进行类比，暗示 Foam 的依赖 VS Code 可能带来类似 Electron 应用的缺点（如资源占用高、笨重等）。这反映了一些用户对 Foam 依赖特定编辑器的潜在担忧。

• [senkora] 提到了 org-roam，这是一个基于 Emacs 和 org-mode 的类似工具，并提供了相关链接。该用户暗示 org-roam 可能是 Foam 的替代选项，特别是对于 Emacs 用户。这指向了不同工具之间的用户偏好和生态系统选择。

补充讨论：
• Foam 的 VS Code 集成特性在用户中引起了不同反应，部分用户认为它对非开发相关的笔记管理不够灵活。
• 用户对工具的数据管理功能（如 Obsidian 的 Dataview）有需求，这可能影响他们是否会选择切换到 Foam。
• 不同的知识管理工具（如 Foam、Obsidian、org-roam）之间的功能对比和用户生态是讨论的另一个焦点。
• 一些用户对 Foam 依赖 VS Code 持保留态度，认为这可能限制其广泛应用。

Foam
👀
This is an early stage project under rapid development. For updates join the
Foam community Discord
! 💬
Foam
is a personal knowledge management and sharing system inspired by
Roam Research
, built on
Visual Studio Code
and
GitHub
.
You can use
Foam
for organising your research, keeping re-discoverable notes, writing long-form content and, optionally, publishing it to the web.
Foam
is free, open source, and extremely extensible to suit your personal workflow. You own the information you create with Foam, and you're free to share it, and collaborate on it with anyone you want.
Features
Graph Visualization
See how your notes are connected via a
graph
with the
Foam: Show Graph
command.
Link Autocompletion
Foam helps you create the connections between your notes, and your placeholders as well.
Sync links on file rename
Foam updates the links to renamed files, so your notes stay consistent.
Unique identifiers across directories
Foam supports files with the same name in multiple directories.
It will use the minimum identifier required, and even report and help you fix existing ambiguous wikilinks.
Link Preview and Navigation
Go to definition, Peek References
See where a note is being referenced in your knowledge base.
Navigation in Preview
Navigate your rendered notes in the VS Code preview panel.
Note embed
Embed the content from other notes.
Support for sections
Foam supports autocompletion, navigation, embedding and diagnostics for note sections.
Just use the standard wiki syntax of
[[resource#Section Title]]
.
Link Alias
Foam supports link aliasing, so you can have a
[[wikilink]]
, or a
[[wikilink|alias]]
.
Templates
Use
custom templates
to have avoid repetitve work on your notes.
Backlinks Panel
Quickly check which notes are referencing the currently active note.
See for each occurrence the context in which it lives, as well as a preview of the note.
Tag Explorer Panel
Tag your notes and navigate them with the
Tag Explorer
.
Foam also supports hierarchical tags.
Orphans and Placeholder Panels
Orphans are notes that have no inbound nor outbound links.
Placeholders are dangling links, or notes without content.
Keep them under control, and your knowledge base in a better state, by using this panel.
Syntax highlight
Foam highlights wikilinks and placeholder differently, to help you visualize your knowledge base.
Daily note
Create a journal with
daily notes
.
Generate references for your wikilinks
Create markdown
references
for
[[wikilinks]]
, to use your notes in a non-Foam workspace.
With references you can also make your notes navigable both in GitHub UI as well as GitHub Pages.
Commands
Explore your knowledge base with the
Foam: Open Random Note
command
Access your daily note with the
Foam: Open Daily Note
command
Create a new note with the
Foam: Create New Note
command
This becomes very powerful when combined with
note templates
and the
Foam: Create New Note from Template
command
See your workspace as a connected graph with the
Foam: Show Graph
command
Recipes
People use Foam in different ways for different use cases, check out the
recipes
page for inspiration!
Getting started
Whether you want to build a
Second Brain
or a
Zettelkasten
, write a book, or just get better at long-term learning,
Foam
can help you organise your thoughts if you follow these simple rules:
Create a single
Foam
workspace for all your knowledge and research following the [[Getting started]] guide.
Write your thoughts in markdown documents (I like to call them
Bubbles
, but that might be more than a little twee). These documents should be atomic: Put things that belong together into a single document, and limit its content to that single topic. (
source
)
Use Foam's shortcuts and autocompletions to link your thoughts together with
[[wikilinks]]
, and navigate between them to explore your knowledge graph.
Get an overview of your
Foam
workspace using the [[Graph Visualisation]], and discover relationships between your thoughts with the use of [
Backlinking
].

• [mtzaldo] 提出了一个技术趋势相关的问题，将 VS Code 和 Electron 进行类比，暗示 Foam 的依赖 VS Code 可能带来类似 Electron 应用的缺点（如资源占用高、笨重等）。这反映了一些用户对 Foam 依赖特定编辑器的潜在担忧。

• [senkora] 提到了 org-roam，这是一个基于 Emacs 和 org-mode 的类似工具，并提供了相关链接。该用户暗示 org-roam 可能是 Foam 的替代选项，特别是对于 Emacs 用户。这指向了不同工具之间的用户偏好和生态系统选择。

补充讨论：
• Foam 的 VS Code 集成特性在用户中引起了不同反应，部分用户认为它对非开发相关的笔记管理不够灵活。
• 用户对工具的数据管理功能（如 Obsidian 的 Dataview）有需求，这可能影响他们是否会选择切换到 Foam。
• 不同的知识管理工具（如 Foam、Obsidian、org-roam）之间的功能对比和用户生态是讨论的另一个焦点。
• 一些用户对 Foam 依赖 VS Code 持保留态度，认为这可能限制其广泛应用。

data.title: Dr. Sbaitso
data.author: bovermyer
data.article_summary: 《Dr. Sbaitso》是1991年由Creative Labs发布的早期人工智能程序，运行于MS-DOS系统，模拟心理治疗对话，让用户与虚拟心理医生互动。该程序通过文本界面与用户交流，依据输入内容作出预设回应，类似于心理咨询，尽管简单，但展示了早期AI的潜力。其直观的键盘和鼠标操作以及全屏模式为用户提供了友好的体验。《Dr. Sbaitso》作为AI发展的重要里程碑，展示了AI在个性化用户体验方面的潜力，并激发了公众对人工智能技术的兴趣，为现代聊天机器人奠定了基础。该程序不仅是怀旧的经典，也代表了人机互动领域的早期创新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Dr. Sbaitso软件的历史、技术影响及用户体验

不同观点：
• [tartoran] 认为Dr. Sbaitso在90年代早期通过简单的程序让人们感觉它具有思考能力，实际上是用户自己在回应问题。他将这一现象与现代的大语言模型（LLMs）进行对比，指出人们仍然倾向于将某种智能投射到这些程序上。

• [omoikane] 更喜欢archive.org上托管的Dr. Sbaitso版本，特别是没有语音的版本，因为运行速度更快。他提供了相关链接，方便其他人体验该软件。

• [teel] 分享了自己在90年代初购买Sound Blaster Pro 2.0声卡的经历，并提到Dr. Sbaitso是他们第一次听到合成语音的技术，特别是用非英语语言输入时，非常有趣。

• [nullc] 表达了对过去计算机操作严格保密的时代的怀念，似乎是在感叹现代技术对隐私的冲击。

• [pimlottc] 提到了另一个演示程序“I’m a talking parrot. Please talk to me!”，提醒大家不要忘记这个同样有趣的程序。

• [anarticle] 认为Dr. Sbaitso是随Sound Blaster卡附赠的一款了不起的软件，在当时拥有声卡非常罕见，大多数电脑只有PC喇叭。他强调了该软件在声音合成和游戏音效支持方面的突破性，并回忆了自己十岁时被其魔力吸引的经历。

• [westurner] 提供了Dr. Sbaitso和Clean Language的维基百科链接，并提到Clean Language问题在相关讨论中的潜在应用价值。

争议焦点：
• 对于Dr. Sbaitso是否真正具有智能的看法存在分歧。一部分人认为程序本身并没有真正的智能，而是用户自己在回应问题；另一部分人则认为现代LLMs与Dr. Sbaitso有相似之处，都是通过用户投射的智能来实现交互。

讨论围绕Dr. Sbaitso的历史背景、技术影响、用户体验和隐私问题展开。参与者分享了个人经历和喜好，同时也涉及到现代技术与过去技术的对比。

Dr. Sbaitso Description
Dr. Sbaitso and A Glimpse into the Early Days of AI
When we think about artificial intelligence today, we might envision complex systems and advanced chatbots like ChatGPT equipped with machine learning. However, the journey of AI began with simpler, yet groundbreaking concepts. One such innovation was
Dr. Sbaitso
—an early artificial intelligence program developed for MS-DOS computers.
Released by Creative Labs in 1991
, Dr. Sbaitso aimed to simulate conversations, inviting users to engage in therapeutic dialogues with a virtual psychologist. Let’s take a deep dive into the world of Dr. Sbaitso and explore its significance in the realm of AI history.
What is Dr. Sbaitso?
The Concept Behind the Program
Dr. Sbaitso was developed to provide a unique interactive experience for users interacting with AI. The program mimics a
psychotherapeutic environment
where users could express their thoughts and feelings, with Dr. Sbaitso responding to those inputs accordingly. This simplicity in conversation models a crucial aspect of early AI, emphasizing user interaction while showcasing the technology available at the time.
How Dr. Sbaitso Works
Operating primarily through a text-based interface, Dr. Sbaitso allows users to type their thoughts, leading to a dialogue that resembles a therapeutic session. The program employs predefined responses, often prompting users with questions such as "WHY DO YOU FEEL THAT WAY?" Despite its limitations, the idea of providing an AI-driven conversation interface laid the groundwork for today's engaging chatbots.
The User Experience with Dr. Sbaitso
Interaction Dynamics
Using Dr. Sbaitso feels like entering the digital office of a psychologist. Users are encouraged to share their emotions, and the program responds with simple yet guiding inquiries. Although the interactions may appear limited by modern standards, this pioneering design offered a glimpse into how future AI systems could evolve toward meaningful conversation.
Accessibility and Controls
The controls for navigating Dr. Sbaitso are straightforward and user-friendly. Players primarily use their keyboards to input text, while mouse support adds convenience for those who prefer point-and-click methods. Additionally, users can switch to full-screen mode with a simple Alt+Enter command, enabling a more immersive experience.
The Significance of Dr. Sbaitso in AI Development
A Historic Milestone
Dr. Sbaitso marks a pivotal moment in the journey of artificial intelligence. As one of the first chatbot programs designed for personal computers, it spotlighted the potential of AI in providing personalized user experiences. At a time before smartphones and sophisticated AI, this program served as an early experiment, contributing to the foundation of conversational interfaces we see today.
Fostering Interest in AI
The novelty of engaging with Dr. Sbaitso captivated users and sparked curiosity about artificial intelligence. Players not only experimented with the program but also pondered the implications of AI in everyday life. As a result, Dr. Sbaitso helped generate public interest in AI technologies, provoking discussions surrounding the role of machines in human interactions.
Reflecting on the Legacy of Dr. Sbaitso
Nostalgia Meets Innovation
For many early computer users, Dr. Sbaitso holds a special place as a nostalgic treasure of the digital past. It represents an era when technology began to weave into the fabric of daily life, offering a taste of what was possible in human-computer interaction. Even today, enthusiasts of retro computing and AI enthusiasts alike revisit this program, reminiscing about the simplicity and curiosity it inspired.
The Journey Forward
The impact of Dr. Sbaitso transcends its basic operational capacities. It serves as a foundation from which modern AI systems and chatbots have evolved. The program's legacy prompts us to reflect on how we can harness technology not just for functionality but also for meaningful connections that enhance our live

data.article_summary: Copilot Spaces旨在解决工程团队知识碎片化问题，通过集中项目相关的代码、文档和自定义指令，使Copilot提供更智能、更相关的回答。团队可以共享这些空间，快速扩展专业知识，提升每个开发者的效率。Spaces让Copilot成为特定领域的专家，提供系统理解、最佳实践等支持，并可自定义指令。代码直接从GitHub仓库添加，保持实时更新。Copilot Spaces目前在GitHub上对所有Copilot用户开放，企业客户需管理员启用预览功能。2025年6月4日起，Spaces将采用与Copilot Chat相同的计费模式。

44187628.article_content:
Back to changelog
Today’s engineering teams struggle with fragmented knowledge. Having critical context scattered across code, documentation, and inside of team members’ heads can make it hard to get up to speed in a new area and get things done. Copilot Spaces solve this by centralizing your project context so Copilot delivers smarter, more relevant responses grounded in your work. This includes items like code, docs, specs, and custom Copilot instructions in the space. You can then share spaces across your GitHub organization to quickly scale expertise and accelerate every developer on your team.
👩‍💻 Turn Copilot into a subject matter expert
Spaces let you ground Copilot’s knowledge in a curated set of specific code, documents, notes, and more. With this extra context, Copilot becomes an expert in the task at hand—from understanding how a system works, to why it was built in a particular way, or even best practice examples. You can also add custom instructions to a space, further tailoring Copilot’s answers in that space.
⚖️ Scale expertise across teams
Use spaces to centralize knowledge and share expertise with teammates. Create a space under your organization and simply share it. Teammates can then work with Copilot in that space, accessing expertise they don’t have and saving them time.
⏲️ Always up to date
Your code is already safely stored on GitHub. Add it to a space by attaching it directly from your repository—no copy and paste needed. Files and repositories added to a space are always kept up to date as they change, making Copilot an evergreen expert in your project.
💬 Get started
Try out Copilot Spaces today at
github.com/copilot/spaces
. This is an early preview. Share what you’re building with us
in the spaces discussion
or using the inline feedback button.
Spaces are currently available in github.com for all Copilot users. If you are a business or enterprise customer, then your organization admin must opt in to
Copilot preview features
.
Starting June 4th, 2025, Copilot Spaces will follow the same billing model as Copilot Chat. For Pro, Pro+, Business, and Enterprise subscribers, spaces chats with a premium model will consume one premium request each, while base model usage will not. For Copilot Free users, spaces chats will count toward their 50 monthly chat limit. Rate limiting may apply during periods of high demand.
Learn more about spaces in
our documentation on Copilot Spaces
.

• **支持存档网站的观点**：  
  doctaj认为archive.ph是一个可靠的工具，可以用来保存和访问可能被删除或更改的网页内容。这有助于保留信息，防止它们在互联网上消失。例如，当原始网页不可用时，存档链接可以提供访问。

• **质疑存档网站准确性的观点**：  
  有些用户可能质疑存档网站是否能够完全准确地保存网页的所有内容，包括动态内容和多媒体元素。虽然存档可以保存文本和静态内容，但对于复杂的网页，可能会有信息丢失或显示不完整的情况。

• **对存档网站合法性的关注**：  
  有观点指出，使用存档网站可能涉及版权和知识产权问题。未经许可保存和提供他人内容可能引发法律争议。一些用户可能因此对使用存档网站持谨慎态度。

data.title: 'Bohemian Rhapsody': The Story Behind Queen's Rule-Breaking Classic Song
data.author: susam
data.article_summary: "Bohemian Rhapsody" originated in the late 1960s as ideas Freddie Mercury jotted down while a student. By the early 1970s, Mercury presented these ideas to his Queen bandmates, initially calling it "The Cowboy Song." The recording process in 1975 was complex, taking place over several studios and involving intricate vocal overdubs, with Mercury meticulously crafting harmonies. The song's structure blends rock and opera, featuring a notable opera section and Mercury's vibrant vocal performances. References in the lyrics, like "Galileo," were personal nods, in this case to guitarist Brian May's interest in astronomy. Despite initial hesitations from their record company about its length, Queen insisted on releasing it as a single. Upon its release in October 1975, it became a huge success, marking a significant moment in music history.

44186283.article_content:
Photo: Queen Productions Ltd
Queen
’s epic rock song “Bohemian Rhapsody” began life sometime in the late 60s, when
Freddie Mercury
was a student at Ealing Art College, starting out as a few ideas for a song scribbled on scraps of paper.
Queen guitarist Brian May remembers the brilliant singer and songwriter giving them the first glimpse in the early 70s of the masterpiece he had at one time called “The Cowboy Song,” perhaps because of the line “Mama… just killed a man.”
“I remember Freddie coming in with loads of bits of paper from his dad’s work, like Post-it notes, and pounding on the piano,” May said in 2008. “He played the piano like most people play the drums. And this song he had was full of gaps where he explained that something operatic would happen here and so on. He’d worked out the harmonies in his head.”
Lenny Kravitz Returning To Las Vegas For Five-Night Residency
Paul McCartney Announces Next Round Of SHM-CD Reissues
Best Albums of 1980: 71 Records You Need To Hear
ADVERTISEMENT
Mercury told bandmates that he believed he had enough material for about three songs but was thinking about blending all the lyrics into one long extravaganza. The final six-minute iconic mini rock opera became the band’s defining song, and eventually provided the title of
the hit 2019 biopic
starring Rami Malek as Mercury.
Queen – Bohemian Rhapsody (Official Video Remastered)
Click to load video
The recording of Bohemian Rhapsody
Queen first properly rehearsed “Bohemian Rhapsody” at Ridge Farm Studio, in Surrey, in mid-1975, and then spent three weeks honing the song at Penrhos Court in Herefordshire. By the summer they were ready to record it; taping began on August 24, 1975 at the famous Rockfield Studios in Monmouth, Wales. It was a moment that May described as “just the biggest thrill.”
The innovative song began with the famous a cappella intro (“Is this the real life?/Is this just fantasy?”) before embracing everything from
glam
-metal rock to opera. A week was devoted to the opera section, for which Mercury had methodically written out all the harmony parts. For the grand chorale, the group layered 160 tracks of vocal overdubs (using 24-track analogue recording), with Mercury singing the middle register, May the low register, and drummer Roger Taylor the high register (John Deacon was on bass guitar but did not sing). Mercury performed with real verve, overdubbing his voice until it sounded like a chorus, with the words “mamma mia”, “Galileo” and “Figaro” bouncing up and down the octaves. “We ran the tape through so many times it kept wearing out,” May said. “Once we held the tape up to the light and we could see straight through it, the music had practically vanished. Every time Fred decided to add a few more ‘Galileo’s we lost something, too.”
The references in Bohemian Rhapsody
Mercury had supposedly written “Galileo” into the lyrics in honor of May, who had a passionate interest in astronomy and would later go on to earn a Ph.D. in astrophysics.
“Bohemian Rhapsody” brims with imaginative language and is a testament to Mercury’s talents as a songwriter. Scaramouche was a buffoonish character in 16th-century commedia dell’arte shows; “Bismillah”, which is taken from the Quran, means “in the name of Allah”; Beelzebub is an archaic name for the devil.
“Freddie was a very complex person; flippant and funny on the surface, but he concealed insecurities and problems in squaring up his life with his childhood,” said May. “He never explained the lyrics, but I think he put a lot of himself into that song.”
Best Queen Songs: 20 Essential Tracks That Weave A Kind Of Magic
10 Things We Learned From The “Bohemian Rhapsody” Biopic
“Queen II” The Album That Elevated The Band To Rock Royalty
The reaction to Bohemian Rhapsody
After the final version was completed – following some refinements at Roundhouse, Sarm East Studios, Scorpio Sound, and Wessex Sound Studios – there was a feeling that Queen had created something special. “Nobody really knew how it was going to sound as a whole six-minute song until it was put together,” producer Roy Thomas Baker told
Performing Songwriter
magazine. “I was standing at the back of the control room, and you just knew that you were listening for the first time to a big page in history. Something inside me told me that this was a red-letter day, and it really was.”
The song, which appears on the album
A Night At The Opera
, was finally released on October 31, 1975, and the impact was instantaneous. “I was green with envy when I heard ‘Bohemian Rhapsody.” It was a piece of sheer originality that took rock and pop away from the normal path,” said Björn Ulvaeus of
ABBA
.
Though the group’s record company were initially reluctant to issue “Bohemian Rhapsody” as a single, Queen were united in insisting that it was the right choice, despite exceeding the three-minute running time expected of most single releases. data.title: NoteGen is a cross-platform Markdown note-taking application
data.article_summary: NoteGen是一款跨平台的Markdown笔记应用，专注于利用AI技术连接记录与写作，将碎片化知识整理为可读笔记。其特点包括：轻量（安装包仅20MB）、无广告、支持多平台（Mac、Windows、Linux，未来还将支持iOS和Android）；多种记录方式（截图、文本、插图、文件、链接等）；原生Markdown格式存储，易于迁移；支持本地离线使用及实时同步到GitHub、Gitee私有仓库，并可回滚历史版本；AI增强功能，支持配置多种模型（如ChatGPT等）；具备录制和写作页面，录制内容可整理后转入写作页面深入编辑；支持文件管理、Markdown编辑、版本控制、AI辅助（对话、润色、翻译等）、全局搜索、主题和多语言等功能。应用现已支持Mac、Windows、Linux，未来将支持移动端。

• [wsc981] 对 JIRA 的看法相对积极，认为其工作良好，但更偏好 Github Issues。同时指出 Azure DevOps 过于复杂，许多功能可以用 Github Actions 替代。此外，对 AWS 服务的复杂性和网站导航体验提出批评。
• [matt_s] 认为 JIRA 受到很多合理的批评，但所有项目跟踪软件都面临同样的问题：过度承诺项目交付时间。认为组织内部的问题不能通过软件解决。

• 工具复杂性：多个评论（Git, Next.js, Azure DevOps, AWS）都提到现代工具和平台的复杂性，以及其对开发者工作效率和体验的影响。

• [esperent] 指出 Next.js 拥有过多的渲染模式和功能（如 SSG, SSR, ISR, PPR 等），并且存在 Vercel 锁定的问题。此外，生态系统碎片化以及应用路由器产生的大量模板代码也是问题。尽管有些部分很优秀，但整体复杂度在增加。
• [wsc981] 对 JIRA 的看法相对积极，认为其工作良好，但更偏好 Github Issues。同时指出 Azure DevOps 过于复杂，许多功能可以用 Github Actions 替代。此外，对 AWS 服务的复杂性和网站导航体验提出批评。
• [matt_s] 认为 JIRA 受到很多合理的批评，但所有项目跟踪软件都面临同样的问题：过度承诺项目交付时间。认为组织内部的问题不能通过软件解决。
• [mattl] 强调周围使用 JIRA 的人都对其不满，并提到浏览器限制从网页表格中复制数据列的问题。

补充讨论：
• [bigyabai] 仅提到 MacOS，可能暗示对该操作系统的关注或不满，但未提供具体论据。

争议焦点：
• JIRA 的优劣：[wsc981] 和 [mattl] 对 JIRA 的评价存在分歧，前者相对满意，后者则强烈不满。
• 工具复杂性：多个评论（Git, Next.js, Azure DevOps, AWS）都提到现代工具和平台的复杂性，以及其对开发者工作效率和体验的影响。

这些观点反映了开发者在使用现代开发工具时面临的复杂性和选择困难，同时也揭示了软件工具在提升效率和增加复杂性之间的权衡。

data.title: US science is being wrecked
data.author: xqcgrek2
data.article_summary: 特朗普政府2026年预算提案大幅削减了资助科学研究的机构预算，导致独特科研设施关闭、支持的科学家数量大幅减少以及多个研究领域停滞。具体包括：NASA的行星科学预算减半，火星样本返回任务被取消，其他科学任务如地球科学和天文学也遭削减；国家科学基金会（NSF）的基础研究资金被大幅削减，生物学、计算机科学、社会科学等领域受影响严重，国际项目削减80%；健康与人类服务部下的NIH预算削减超40%，并进行重组；能源部则取消了对风能、太阳能和可再生能源的资助。整体来看，这些削减将对美国科学界造成长期损害。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对科学投资和预算削减的不同看法

不同观点：
• **支持对科学投资进行审视的观点**：[sQL_inject]认为，反对预算削减的人也应该关注哪些历史投资有良好的回报率。他提出，科学界应开放审视这些组织的资金使用情况，特别是在债务危机的背景下，需要评估这些组织的资金与成功比例是否适当。例子包括比较用于火星岩石研究和用于核聚变能源研究的资金价值。

• **批评实用主义思维的观点**：[rotten]将支持削减预算的观点比作“我从不在工作中使用代数，但用了足球教练教的东西”的心态，暗示这种实用主义忽视了基础科学研究的长远价值。

• **对国家前景感到悲观的观点**：[rossant]表达了对国家未来感到悲观的看法，形容当前的情况像是“一个国家的慢动作自杀”。

• **将预算削减与政治立场挂钩的观点**：[mandeepj]认为，削减科学和教育预算与“法西斯主义者不喜欢科学和教育”有关，暗示这些削减反映了更广泛的政治倾向。

• **指责外部资金影响的观点**：[graymatters]提到，一些组织接受卡塔尔资金用于推广卡塔尔议程，暗示这些组织在资金接受上不够审慎，可能因此导致当前的预算削减。

• **认为政客腐败导致预算浪费的观点**：[billy99k]指出，浪费纳税人资金的是政客在洗钱和欺诈上的行为，暗示预算削减是因为这些组织被故意用作政治工具，以保护某些政治利益。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于科学投资的优先级和回报率，以及外部政治和资金影响如何干扰科学组织的正常运作。
• 讨论还涉及到对国家未来和政治动机的广泛担忧，特别是科学和教育预算削减背后的政治因素。

WASHINGTON, DC—The general outline of the Trump administration's proposed 2026 budget was released a few weeks back, and it included massive cuts for most agencies, including
every one that funds scientific research
. Late last week, those agencies began releasing details of what the cuts would mean for the actual projects and people they support. And the results are as bad as the initial budget had suggested: one-of-a-kind scientific experiment facilities and hardware retired, massive cuts in supported scientists, and entire areas of research halted.
And this comes in an environment where previously funded grants are being terminated, funding is being held up for ideological screening, and universities have been subject to arbitrary funding freezes. Collectively, things are heading for damage to US science that will take decades to recover from. It's a radical break from the trajectory science had been on.
That's the environment that the US's National Academies of Science found itself in yesterday while hosting the
State of the Science
event in Washington, DC. It was an obvious opportunity for the nation's leading scientific organization to warn the nation of the consequences of the path that the current administration has been traveling. Instead, the event largely ignored the present to worry about a future that may never exist.
The proposed cuts
The
top-line budget numbers
proposed earlier indicated things would be bad: nearly 40 percent taken off the National Institutes of Health's budget, the National Science Foundation down by over half. But now, many of the details of what those cuts mean are becoming apparent.
NASA's budget
includes sharp cuts for planetary science, which would be cut in half and then stay flat for the rest of the decade, with the
Mars Sample Return mission
canceled. All other science budgets, including Earth Science and Astrophysics, take similar hits; one astronomer posted a graphic showing how many present and future missions that would mean. Active missions that have returned unprecedented data, like
Juno
and
New Horizons
, would go, as would two Mars orbiters. As
described by Science magazine's news team
, "The plans would also kill off nearly every major science mission the agency has not yet begun to build."
A chart prepared by astronomer Laura Lopez showing just how many astrophysics missions will be cancelled.
Credit:
Laura Lopez
The National Science Foundation, which funds much of the US's fundamental research, is also
set for brutal cuts
. Biology, engineering, and education will all be slashed by over 70 percent; computer science, math and physical science, and social and behavioral science will all see cuts of over 60 percent. International programs will take an 80 percent cut. The funding rate of grant proposals is expected to drop from 26 percent to just 7 percent, meaning the vast majority of grants submitted to the NSF will be a waste of time. The number of people involved in NSF-funded activities will drop from over 300,000 to just 90,000. Almost every program to broaden participation in science will be eliminated.
As for specifics, they're equally grim. The fleet of research ships will essentially become someone else's problem: "The FY 2026 Budget Request will enable partial support of some ships." We've been able to better pin down the nature and location of gravitational wave events as detectors in Japan and Italy joined the original two LIGO detectors; the NSF will reverse that progress by shutting one of the LIGOs. The NSF's contributions to detectors at the Large Hadron Collider will be cut by over half, and one of the two very large telescopes it was helping fund will be cancelled (say goodbye to the Thirty Meter Telescope). "Access to the telescopes at Kitt Peak and Cerro Tololo will be phased out," and the NSF will transfer the facilities to other organizations.
The Department of Health and Human Services has been
less detailed
about the specific cuts its divisions will see, largely focusing on the overall numbers, which are down considerably. The NIH, which is facing a cut of over 40 percent, will be reorganized, with its 19 institutes pared down to just eight. This will result in some odd pairings, such as the dental and eye institutes ending up in the same place; genomics and biomedical imaging will likewise end up under the same roof. Other groups like the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Food and Drug Administration will also face major cuts.
Issues go well beyond the core science agencies, as well. In the
Department of Energy
, funding for wind, solar, and renewable grid integration has been zeroed out, essentially ending all programs in this area. Hydrogen and fuel cells face a similar fate. Collectively, these had gotten over $600 billion dollars in 2024's budget. Other areas of science at th

data.article_summary: 《Microsoft 365 Copilot实验：跨政府部门成果报告》由政府数字服务（GDS）发布，总结了2024年9月30日至12月31日进行的大规模实验。该实验评估了Microsoft 365 Copilot（一款集成于Word、Excel、PowerPoint、Outlook和Teams的AI助理）对工作效率和用户满意度的影响，具体包括是否能提升任务质量、减少日常工作时间和降低任务完成难度。实验覆盖了12个政府机构的20,000名员工，是迄今为止英国政府范围内最大规模的M365 Copilot部署。报告于2025年6月2日发布，详细分析了为期三个月的实验对生产力、效率和用户满意度的具体影响。

The Government Digital Service (GDS) conducted a large-scale experiment with Microsoft 365 Copilot from 30 September to 31 December 2024.
M365 Copilot is an AI-powered assistant integrated into Microsoft’s productivity tools, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams. The experiment evaluated whether AI tools could:
improve user satisfaction at work- reduce effort required to complete tasks

reduce time spent on routine activities
This report presents the findings and examines the impact on productivity, efficiency and user satisfaction during a three-month experiment.

data.title: New 30TB tape is a welcome moment for petabyte-scale storage
data.author: miles
data.article_summary: Symply发布了全球首款LTO-10磁带存储系列，LTO-10磁带拥有30TB原生容量（75TB压缩），相比最初计划的48TB有所缩减。LTO技术路线图计划未来达到576TB，预计到2040年实现。虽然LTO-10的容量比LTO-9提升了67%，但低于此前预期。LTO-10保持400MB/s的传输速率，填满一盘磁带大约需要一天时间。Symply将于2025年6月开始发售LTO-10产品，起价为11,995美元。IBM和Spectra Logic也宣布支持LTO-10。尽管面临硬盘和新兴存储技术竞争，LTO磁带因其适应性和性价比，依然在存储市场中占据重要地位。

44187204.article_content:
Symply Launches the World’s First LTO-10 Tape Storage Range - YouTube
Watch On
10th generation LTO is finally here, four years after 9th gen launched
It will have a 30TB capacity, far less than the 48TB originally planned
LTO roadmap runs to 576TB which may not appear until 2040 at the current rate
If you want to back up tens of petabytes of data or even more, here’s some good news for you. Without much fanfare, IBM, Symply and Spectra Logic have separately made LTO-10 announcements in the past 48 hours.
Announced in 2014, LTO-10 is the 10th iteration of Linear Tape Open technology. This tape media can now reach 30TB native capacity and a staggering 75TB compressed (using the industry standard of 2.5:1 ratio).
Even more surprising is that the transfer rate remained at 400MB/s whereby incremental speed improvements were the norm in the previous nine generations. In theory, filling up an entire tape would take a bit less than a day.
You may like
MagStor has launched the world's first Thunderbolt 5 LTO tape drive, but it won’t be cheap
Seagate CEO hints at 150TB hard drives thanks to novel 15TB platters, but notes it won't happen for another decade
Seagate confirms 40TB hard drives have already been shipped, but don't expect them to go on sale anytime soon
LTO’s taking its time
Even if 30TB sounds fantastic, it is significantly smaller than what was originally proposed.
Eight years ago
when the LTO organization published their Ultrium roadmap, it listed the LTO-10 as being a 48TB model, that dropped to 36TB in the most recent one, from 2022, and now the actual product launched with ‘only’ 30TB.
That is
67% higher than the capacity of the new LTO-9 tape (18TB)
but only 25% higher than that of the old LTO-9 purported tape capacity (24TB). In other words, six LTO-10 tapes can replace 10 LTO-9 tapes.
Back then, the LTO consortium told us, “Doubling capacity approximately every two years is still technically feasible for LTO tape technology and the LTO Program anticipates being able to return to that pattern in future generations”.
Why? Perhaps because the legacy (hard drives) and exotic competitions (ceramic, DNA, silica) aren’t as compelling as originally planned. The
first 30TB hard drive launched in January 2024
with
100TB hard drives expected to debut by 2030
.
LTO-9 hit the market in September 2021
and was delayed by a series of setbacks.
Are you a pro? Subscribe to our newsletter
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
What’s next for LTO?
So one can expect LTO-11 to launch sometime in 2029. LTO’s latest roadmap goes up to LTO-14 with a native capacity of 576TB but this document will almost certainly be changed because of LTO-10’s unexpected (and disappointing) capacity change.
Symply, a storage hardware expert that launched the first LTO-9 tape drive, will start shipping LTO-10 products as early as mid-June 2025 from $11,995 (SAS) with devices equiped with other interfaces (Ethernet and Thunderbolt) costing more.
Symply told TechRadar Pro that they will provide pricing details for LTO-10 media soon. They also told us “the LTO-10 media is 1035m in length which is the same as LTO-9. It is a high density on the media that enable the higher capacity.”
LTO-9 is currently the cheapest of the LTO family, costing around $5 per TB; a 30TB tape would likely sell for more than $150.
IBM, one of the founders of LTO, has also announced an LTO 10 tape drive,
while Spectra Logic
announced support for the new media
.
25 years and still going strong
It’s been a quarter of a century already since LTO-1 hit the market and while it has many critics (
including within the US government
), its resilience, value for money and ability to adapt to countless storage demands makes it a reliable partner regardless of the use case.
We witnessed the demise of competitors (like
Sony’s ODA
) and while alternative forms of storage (
most notably Cerabyte
) show exciting potential, they are still very far from reaching the same status as tape.

data.title: Precious Plastic is in trouble
data.author: diggan
data.article_summary: Precious Plastic，一个旨在全球推广塑料回收的开放资源项目，正面临生存危机。自2020年发布第四版以来，该项目通过与全球超过100名志愿者合作，开发了专业机器、工作坊启动包等，并在2023年实现了显著影响：1100个组织在56个国家回收了140万公斤塑料，创造了370万美元的收入。然而，项目面临三大问题：首先，因新冠疫情和建筑问题，团队失去了工作空间；其次，项目缺乏可持续的商业模式，无法在不与社区竞争的情况下产生足够收入；最后，团队遭遇法律诉讼，进一步加剧了财务困境。这些挑战使得项目难以为继，急需找到解决方案以继续推进使命。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Precious Plastic组织的运营、透明度、未来方向以及其在塑料回收领域的实际作用和影响

• [ljm] 认为该组织虽然收到了大量捐款，但选择将资金用于社区项目而非解决组织内部问题。他质疑组织的领导层是否真正反思过错误，并担心捐款可能被用于不透明的用途，甚至可能是骗局。

This is a heavy message to send, but essential for the future of Precious Plastic. It will either make it or not. In this post Iâll give a detailed overview of all the current problems we have, how it got to this point and whats next. A short summarised video is below. No

Our last big development

Lets start with our last big development. Â 2020, when we released Version 4, this was our latest release. We worked about 1,5 year with over +100 people from around the world. We developed the first âProâ Machines, a Sheetpress, Starterkits, Business calculators, new moulds, products and more. Looking back this was quite a unique moment. A lot of passionate work was done by volunteers and everything was shared Open Source online for free. Here some of the things we made
With a relatively small amount of money, we reached a global impact in 2023 of over 1100 organzations in 56 countries, who recycled 1.400.000KG Plastic, they generated together a revenue of +$3.7 Million, employed 530 people, works with 3.405 volunteers and built 1.175 machines. How we work
In order to understand our problems itâs important to know how Precious Plastic is developed since its unusual. We work in what we call Versions. Version 1 got released in 2013 and the latest one 4 years ago. The principle is, we develop a lot of new things, share them online for free. And then whoever was involved takes a holiday or goes off to something else. They really have to go because at that point we spend all our money. The workspace is empty, the work drops, nothing new is made, we wait. Up until now for some magical reason we always received a gift to continue moving forward. From winning awards, to getting a big workspace donated. Whenever we got enough resources we assembled a team and started developing again.. Each time the team and amount of work grew. Until the latest version, here the problems started.
When the Problems started
â
We worked in versions not because we wanted to, but because we had to. We share everything online for free because we believe recycling knowledge should be available for everyone. As a consequence we donât generate enough income to pay a team all year around. But after Version 4 a small group of seven dedicated ambitious volunteers wanted to try and sustain Precious Plastic all year around. So we can continue development and have a bigger impact to reduce plastic waste. This by itself is a hard job but we also had some extra problems on the way
â
#1 No workspace
â
The team was ready to continue work. But just a few weeks later Covid-19 came to the world, but this wasnât our main problem. Our problem was Chrome-6, a chemical the municipality found in the paint from the building that was applied 40 years ago. Which meant we had to leave the workspace fast, and the building was large, we had a lot of machines and items to sell, in a short amount of time, during lockdowns. This meant we had to sell many things below value since that period most people were looking to buy bread machines, not robot arms. After the exhausting/rushed job of leaving our workspace we could stay in the garage/shed in the house of one of the team members in France. It was nice we had a base to continue, but it was much smaller and temporary. It was quite a downgrade.
#2 No business model
â
One of the main goals of this small team was trying to find a business model that would serve Precious Plasticâs mission, bring income to sustain a team and not compete with the rest of the community. The last one is difficult, because our most logical and common model would be to sell machines and moulds. There are not many Open Source Hardware projects like Precious Plastic in the world. And the ones that exist mostly sell their products. Arduino sells their circuit boards, Prusa sells 3d printers. However in our case weâre also building a global network of machine builders that can provide local recycling equipment. We didn't want to compete with our own community.
The plan was to do Projects or as we called them, Collabs. It meant to help others set up their projects. Sort of a consultancy. The team setup quite a few cool projects, from a refugee camp in a desert in Algeria to a big Sheetpress in Nigeria. And meanwhile released a few new machine drawings. The model somewhat worked, we continued development and could do meaningful work. However it was financially always tight and often didnât bring in enough money to sustain the team (that was getting paid minimum Dutch wage). But what really broke it was the next problem
â
#3 Lawsuit

data.title: Japan's births in 2024 fall below 700k for first time
data.author: ivewonyoung
data.article_summary: 2024年，日本的新生儿数量首次降至70万以下，为686,061人，同比减少5.7%。总生育率也创下历史新低，降至1.15。这一趋势已持续九年，且下降速度比政府预期提前15年。虽然结婚数量在2024年有所增加，但死亡人数达到1,605,298人，创战后新高，自然减少人数为919,237人。东京生育率最低，为0.96，而冲绳最高，为1.54。专家原预计2039年出生数才会降至68万范围。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日本战后死亡人数和人口自然减少的问题

不同观点：
• [duxup] 引用了数据，指出日本报告的死亡人数为1,605,298，是战后时期最高的，同时人口自然减少（死亡人数减去出生人数）达到了创纪录的919,237，连续18年人口呈现下降趋势。这表明日本正面临严重的人口减少问题，且趋势明显。

• [mensetmanusman] 对此数据的未来影响进行了调侃，提出通过在当前数字上“增加两个零并减去15%”来估算一个人死亡时的总人口。这暗示对未来人口大幅减少的担忧，并可能认为当前的趋势将持续并加剧。

补充讨论：
- [duxup] 的数据引用表明了日本当前人口问题的严峻性，重点在于死亡人数和出生人数之间的巨大差距。
- [mensetmanusman] 的评论则带有一种悲观预测的色彩，通过一种假设性的计算方式表达了对未来人口下降趋势的看法。
- 争议的焦点可能在于如何有效应对这种人口减少的趋势，以及对未来人口估算的准确性和潜在社会经济影响的讨论。

44187325.article_content:
This unrelated photo shows a newborn at a clinic in Otsu, Shiga Prefecture, in June 11, 2022. (Mainichi)
TOKYO (Kyodo) -- The number of births in Japan fell below 700,000 for the first time in 2024, declining 5.7 percent from the previous year to 686,061, government data showed Wednesday, highlighting a continued trend of delayed marriages and childbirths.
Japan's total fertility rate -- the average number of children a woman is estimated to bear in her lifetime -- also fell to a record-low 1.15, down from 1.20 in 2023, according to the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare.
Both the number of births and the fertility rate have decreased for nine consecutive years. The pace of Japan's declining birthrate is now 15 years ahead of government projections.
The full-year figures exclude babies born to foreign nationals.
The number of marriages, a key factor influencing future birth trends, increased for the first time in two years in 2024 to 485,063, up by 10,322 from a year earlier.
A total of 1,605,298 deaths were reported, the highest number in the postwar period, while the natural decrease -- deaths minus births -- reaching a record 919,237, marking a decline for the 18th straight year.
Japan's birthrate has been falling since hitting a peak during the second baby boom in 1973, when around 2.09 million births were recorded. The figure fell below 1 million in 2016 and below 800,000 in 2022.
The National Institute of Population and Social Security Research had not projected births to drop into the 680,000 range until 2039.
By prefecture, Tokyo recorded the lowest fertility rate at 0.96, followed by Miyagi at 1.00 and Hokkaido at 1.01. Okinawa in southern Japan had the highest rate at 1.54, followed by Fukui at 1.46.

data.title: Bookish Diversions: Reading as Help for Living
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了通过阅读小说来帮助处理复杂生活决策的观点。作者Joel J. Miller引用了Steven Johnson的《Farsighted》一书，指出小说如乔治·艾略特的《 Middlemarch 》可以帮助读者练习应对多维度和多层次的决策。小说不仅提供了对潜在事件的模拟，还通过角色的内心活动让读者更好地理解人类情感和认知。这不仅有助于自我反思，还能为现实生活中的决策提供智慧。此外，作者还提到，阅读经典小说如《Jane Eyre》、《Anna Karenina》等，可以提升对智力卓越性的欣赏，尽管对提升个人道德的直接作用存疑。总的来说，小说作为一种自我反思的工具，能够帮助读者更好地理解自己和周围世界。
